\begin{refsection}
\section{Research Context}
Research question: Is the named-chunk notation used in these lecture
notes literate programming, is literate programming an established
practice, and did it originate with Knuth's 1984 paper? Relevant papers
concern writing a program as a document for human readers from which
code is extracted (tangling) and a typeset document is produced
(weaving), tools that implement this, empirical or experience reports on
using it, its adoption in reproducible research and computational
notebooks, or criticism of it (limited adoption, maintenance cost,
tooling burden). Category tags to assign exactly one of: supports-claim
= the paper bears on the claim and supports it; qualifies-claim = the
paper bears on the claim but contradicts, narrows or complicates it;
adjacent-subtopic = same field, different question; off-topic-false-hit
= another field, keyword overlap only.
